title: Someone rang claiming to be IT and asked her to install a remote tool

review.authored_by: claude-opus-5 (Claude Code session) — drafted from the runbooks, the triage prompt's definitions and decide.ts, not from system output

conversation.author: requester
conversation.body:
Somebody rang about twenty minutes ago saying he was from IT and that my laptop
was sending out spam. He wanted me to go to a website and install something
called AnyDesk so he could clear it.

I did not do it and I hung up. He knew my name and that I am in Finance.

Worth telling you about?

Priya

handling.escalation_reason: An attempted social-engineering call against a named finance user; security decides whether anyone else was called.

rationale: Nothing happened, and it still goes to a person. Two independent reasons converge: an attempted compromise is security-sensitive under G3, which forces at least P2 even though her work is entirely unaffected, and she is a VIP with vip_always_human on (G5). The expected rule is security_sensitive because rule 2 sits above the VIP rule at 4 - so this case cannot be used as evidence that the VIP rule works, which is what case-093 is for. The detail worth keeping is that he knew her name and department: that is a targeted call, and a targeted call against the Financial Controller is the opening move of an invoice fraud.
